Use a unique, strong password for every account — consider a password manager.
Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) wherever it's available.
Never click on links or attachments from unknown or suspicious emails.
Keep your operating system, browser, and apps updated regularly.
Avoid logging into bank or email accounts over public Wi-Fi.
Check the URL carefully before entering any personal information.
Back up your important files regularly to protect against ransomware.
Be cautious of urgent or threatening messages demanding immediate action — that's a common scam tactic.
Use a VPN when connecting to unsecured or public networks.
Review app permissions periodically and remove access you don't need.
Never share your OTP or password with anyone, even if they claim to be support staff.
Look for HTTPS and a padlock icon before entering sensitive data on a website.
Log out of accounts on shared or public computers.
Regularly monitor your bank statements for unauthorized transactions.
Be skeptical of unexpected prize, lottery, or inheritance emails — they're almost always scams.
Use antivirus/anti-malware software and keep it updated.
Think before you post — oversharing personal info online can aid identity theft.
Verify unknown callers or emails claiming to be from your bank by contacting them directly through official channels.
Lock your devices with a PIN, password, or biometric authentication.
Disable Bluetooth and Wi-Fi when not in use to reduce attack surface.
